files.purpose: Gives any view a right-click or control-click context menu rendered as the app's own PopoverMenu at the pointer, using a transparent AppKit overlay that claims only secondary clicks so text selection, links, buttons and drags in the SwiftUI content underneath behave exactly as if it were absent.
key_symbols: private final class RightClickCatcherView: NSView with hitTest(_:), rightMouseDown(with:), mouseDown(with:), rightMouseUp(with:), isFlipped, mouseDownCanMoveWindow, acceptsFirstMouse(for:)
state_owned: RightClickPopoverModifier: @State private var anchor: CGPoint?, where nil means the popover is closed
RightClickCatcherView: var onRightClick: (CGPoint) -> Void, refreshed in updateNSView
side_effects: Presents a SwiftUI popover; no disk, network, process, timer or notification work
platform_assumptions: AppKit NSView subclass bridged through NSViewRepresentable
NSApp.currentEvent inspected inside hitTest to decide whether the overlay claims the click at all
isFlipped = true so the reported point is in top-left coordinates matching SwiftUI
mouseDownCanMoveWindow = false so a secondary click here never drags the window
acceptsFirstMouse(for:) = true so the menu opens on the first click into an inactive window
macOS convention that control plus left click is a secondary click
ui_elements: Popover presented with attachmentAnchor: .rect(.rect(CGRect(origin: anchor ?? .zero, size: CGSize(width: 1, height: 1)))) and arrowEdge: .top, so it hangs off a 1 by 1 rect at the pointer
Popover content is PopoverMenu { RowActionItems(actions: actions()) }
The catcher is attached with .overlay { RightClickCatcher { point in anchor = point } }, covering the whole view
init?(coder:) is marked @available(*, unavailable) and returns nil
feature_notes: hitTest returns nil for every event that is not a right mouse-down or a control plus left mouse-down, and also nil when the converted point is outside bounds, so the overlay is invisible to normal interaction
The presentation binding closes the popover by setting anchor back to nil when SwiftUI reports dismissal
rightMouseDown converts event.locationInWindow into the catcher's flipped coordinates before calling onRightClick
mouseDown only intercepts when .control is held; otherwise it calls super.mouseDown
rightMouseUp is overridden to do nothing, suppressing AppKit's own handling on mouse up
actions is an escaping closure evaluated when the popover is built, so the menu reflects state at the moment of the click
unresolved_questions: RowAction's fields and how RowActionItems renders them (titles, symbols, destructive roles) are defined outside this bundle
Which views actually apply .rightClickPopover is not visible from this file alone
Whether the 1 by 1 anchor rect shifts the popover arrow noticeably near a view's edges cannot be determined without running the app
